title: Spanish A1: Ordering at a café in Spain
subtitle: Understand the waiter, order politely, ask for the bill, and choose tú or usted

learner.topic: Beginner Spanish (CEFR A1): ordering food and drink at a café or bar in Spain
goals: Understand a short café exchange with a waiter
Order food and drink politely, including quantities and simple preferences
Ask for the bill and respond to common questions
Choose correctly between tú and usted in this setting
learner.scope: CEFR A1, café/bar service encounters in Spain only

learner.background: Synthetic profile: adult English speaker travelling to Madrid in two months

constraints: Target language: Spanish as spoken in Spain (es-ES)

practice.realWorld: Weekly speaking practice with a friend who speaks Spanish; no microphone tools

sources.evidenceStandard: Council of Europe CEFR descriptors; Instituto Cervantes Plan curricular; RAE / Diccionario panhispánico de dudas for usage

assumptions: Synthetic learner profile (adult English speaker, true beginner, travelling to Madrid); no personal data.
Spanish of Spain (es-ES). Other varieties (e.g. Latin American vosotros/ustedes, voseo) are out of scope.

Primary sources (RAE/DPD, Council of Europe, Instituto Cervantes) could not be fetched when this course was written (HTTP 403 / maintenance redirect). Claims about usage are therefore marked as course decisions or simplifications, not as verified RAE statements. See each lesson's sources.
Menu items and prices in examples are illustrative, not a real menu. Real cafés differ by region and venue.
Speech synthesis, where the browser offers it, is a synthetic voice and not a native-speaker model. No microphone tools are used.
Two lessons (about 40 minutes of content) are developed; the 3-hour target is met only after the planned lessons in PROGRESS.md are written.

outcomes.text: Understand the gist and the key questions of a short café exchange with a waiter (greeting, "what will you have", "anything else", "for here or to go")
Order food and drink politely, including quantities (1-4) and simple preferences (with/without, to take away), in a typed or spoken turn
Ask for the bill, say whether you pay by card or cash, and answer common questions from the waiter
Choose tú or usted for a given café situation and form the matching verb (quieres/quiere), explaining the choice

modules.summary: Understand the waiter and order drinks and food politely.

modules.title: The bill, and tú vs usted
modules.summary: Ask for the bill, answer routine questions, and pick the right form of address.

glossary.definition: The informal "you" (singular). Verb: second person singular, e.g. quieres.
The formal "you" (singular). Although it means "you", its verb is third person singular, e.g. quiere. Source: es.wikipedia (citing RAE/DPD); see lesson sources.
Using tú (and its verb forms) to address someone.
Waiter / waitress. Masculine camarero, feminine camarera.
The bill. Core phrase: "La cuenta, por favor." Not verified against DLE in this course (source blocked).
Please. Works with both tú and usted.
The ending a verb takes depending on who does the action. querer: yo quiero, tú quieres, usted quiere.

intro:
You will be in Madrid in two months. This course trains one real situation: a short service encounter at a café or bar. You will read and hear a waiter's typical questions, order food and drink with quantities and simple preferences, ask for the bill, and decide whether to say tú or usted.

How it works: each lesson takes about 20 minutes and mixes dialogues, typed answers, fill-in-the-blank exercises and sorting tasks. The app can check typed answers against a list of accepted variants, but it cannot judge pronunciation or tone. For speaking, each lesson ends with a practice task for your weekly session with your Spanish-speaking friend, with criteria your friend can use.

Status: version 0.1 contains two complete lessons; more are planned.

diagnostic.intro: Two quick questions. They only suggest a pace; nothing is hidden.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is the most natural way to ask for a coffee with milk politely?
options: Yo soy un café con leche.
questions.explanation: A short noun phrase plus "por favor" is a normal polite order.

feedback.1: "Soy" means "I am": it says you ARE a coffee.
feedback.2: Missing "con" and no article; not a sentence a waiter expects.

questions.prompt: In "¿Qué quiere tomar?" the waiter is using…
questions.explanation: "Quiere" is third person singular, the verb form that goes with usted.

capstone.title: A full café visit with your friend
capstone.task: With your Spanish-speaking friend playing the waiter, act out a complete visit: greet, order two different drinks and one food item with one preference, answer one question ("¿Algo más?" or "¿Para tomar aquí o para llevar?"), ask for the bill, and pay. Do it once with the friend using usted and once using tú, and reply appropriately.

descriptors: Needed most questions repeated or translated
Understood routine questions after one repeat
Understood routine questions the first time
Single words only, no por favor
Complete order with por favor, small errors in articles or quantity
Complete, polite order with correct quantity and one preference
Could not ask for the bill
Asked for the bill; answered with prompting
Asked for the bill and answered card/cash and other questions unprompted
Correct forms and can explain why in one sentence

capstone.evaluation: Self-assessment is only part of the evidence here. Ask your friend to rate each criterion independently and to tell you one thing that sounded unnatural. The app cannot evaluate speech.
capstone.model: Waiter: Buenas tardes. ¿Qué le pongo? You: Buenas tardes. Un café con leche y una caña, por favor. Y una tortilla. Waiter: ¿Algo más? You: Nada más, gracias. ... You: La cuenta, por favor. Waiter: ¿Efectivo o tarjeta? You: Con tarjeta. (Illustrative; real phrasing varies.)
